project.title: Brightdock: the deploy log your team can read

audio.music: one steady electronic pulse, about 100 bpm, cuts on the beat, added in the edit

series_lock.character: no people on screen; the product's own interface is the subject of every shot
series_lock.environment: Brightdock's dark interface on a near-black ground, one panel per shot in the lower two-thirds, the upper third left empty
series_lock.lighting: flat screen light, a faint lime glow at the top and bottom edges of the frame
series_lock.color_grade: no grade: near-black #0B0D10, off-white #F4F5F0, one lime accent #C8F250; red and amber only as deploy status inside the product

shots.subject: a wall of raw deploy log lines in grey monospaced type filling the lower two-thirds, one line marked in red where a health check failed, the lines fading out at the top and bottom
shots.rationale: The opening has to show the problem before it is named: nobody can read this. The one red line gives the eye a place to land, and the empty upper third is where the question goes.

shots.subject: the Brightdock deploy list: a panel headed Deploys with six rows, each a deploy number, what it was, the service, who shipped it and when, a lime dot for live and one amber row that was rolled back
shots.rationale: The cut from the log wall to one tidy list is the whole pitch, so the list arrives on the first hard cut and holds for three and a half seconds, long enough to read two rows.

shots.subject: one deploy open: the number 214 set very large, the service name beside it, a lime live status, then three changes each with lines added and removed, and who merged it
shots.rationale: Step one of the walk-through: open one deploy. The number is the largest thing in any frame of the film, so the viewer knows where they are without reading.

shots.subject: a deploy that failed its health check, marked with a red dot, a wide lime button to roll back to the deploy before it with a cursor on it, and under it a line with a tick saying the earlier deploy is live again
shots.rationale: Step two: the thing people buy it for. The button is the one lime element and fills the width of the panel, so the action reads at thumb size.

shots.subject: three notices stacked and fading back: the newest says deploy 214 is live and who shipped it, the ones behind it say an earlier deploy was rolled back and another went live
shots.rationale: Step three: the rest of the team. Three seconds is enough because the frame is one sentence repeated three times at falling contrast.

shots.subject: the Brightdock mark, a lime rounded square with three dark bars, centred in the lower half with the product name under it on the near-black ground
shots.rationale: The result is the product named in one line. The mark sits low so the line owns the upper third, and the address is a lockup so it does not compete with it.
